description: Gating backfill program (79-band). Today the gate is real but sparse: only 24 of the 245 seed notebooks are gated, so 221 notebooks are browsable-but-ungated (a topic with no checks gates nothing, by design — praxis/progress.py). This band drives the remaining ~221 to gated by REUSING THE SHIPPED CHECK MACHINERY UNCHANGED — praxis/checks.py (checks_from_reply -> grade -> write) over GATED_SECTIONS, and the derived-unlock gate in progress.py — run in per-domain batches across the 14 domains rather than one sweep, with the anti-fabrication verification (the reference `solution` run against its own `test` in a subprocess) held as the quality bar it already enforces. It invents no new gating primitive; it runs the shipped one at scale. REVISED 2026-08-11 by decision D10 (rosetta/strategy/DECISIONS.md): the format this band writes at scale is nbgrader's cell-level schema, adopted in `84-nbgrader-cell-schema-adoption`, NOT the parallel `<slug>.checks.json` sidecar this band was originally written against — backfilling 221 notebooks into a format that is about to be retired would be the single most expensive way to discover the adoption. Hence the hard dependency on 84: the schema lands first, the backfill runs against it, and `nbgrader validate` is the bar every backfilled notebook must clear. PRIORITIZE BREADTH-FIRST, SHALLOW GATING: the differentiator is largely unshipped at 24/245, so coverage across all 14 domains beats depth in a few — a shallow but real gate on every domain moves the product further than an exhaustive one on three. Anti-fabrication: a checkset that fails the grader is never written (same rule as the constructor), and an already-gated notebook is skipped not rewritten — so a batch is resumable and idempotent exactly like construction; the coverage number only moves for notebooks that gained a real, validate-passing gate.
warmup: echo '--- the machinery to reuse, unchanged ---'; grep -n 'def checks_from_reply\|def checkset_failures\|def needs_checks\|GATED_SECTIONS\|verify_code' praxis/checks.py | head
echo '--- the one batch loop ---'; sed -n '443,500p' praxis/construct.py
echo '--- reality: 24 gated of 245 ---'; echo "gated: $(find notebooks -name '*.checks.json' | wc -l)  total: $(find notebooks -name '*.ipynb' | wc -l)"

userStories.title: Gate one domain's notebooks by reusing the shipped check machinery
acceptanceCriteria: A per-domain backfill drives every ungated ✅ notebook in one domain to gated by calling the shipped path — construct_topic(..., checks=True) / checks.py over GATED_SECTIONS — with NO rewrite of the gating primitive, writing 84's adopted NBGRADER CELL SCHEMA (graded/solution/locked cells with stable `grade_id`s, hidden tests via nbgrader's delimiters) and never a parallel checkset format.

It is idempotent: a notebook that is already gated is skipped not rewritten (the needs_checks() contract, re-expressed against the nbgrader schema), and a notebook that is not yet ✅ is left for construction rather than force-gated, so the batch is resumable exactly like construct_each.

The anti-fabrication bar is held: a gate is written only when `nbgrader validate` passes AND the reference solution actually runs against its own test in a subprocess; a notebook that fails is not written and stays ungated.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes and `nbgrader validate` passes on the backfilled notebooks, including a test that backfilling a domain fixture writes a valid, validate-passing gate for an ungated topic and skips an already-gated one.

userStories.title: Batch the backfill across the 14 domains, resumably
acceptanceCriteria: A batch entry point runs the per-domain backfill across all 14 domains (a one-liner over the shipped construct_each, the way construct_domain / construct_subject already are), so the whole ~221-notebook backlog can be driven in domain-sized batches rather than one sweep.

The ORDER IS BREADTH-FIRST across the 14 domains, not depth-first within one: the batch entry point drives a shallow pass over every domain before deepening any, so coverage climbs across the whole library rather than perfecting three domains while eleven stay ungated. The chosen order is documented and the per-domain fractions after the first breadth pass are recorded in progress.txt.

The run is resumable and safe to re-invoke: re-running skips domains/notebooks already gated and never clobbers a passing gate, so an interrupted batch resumes without redoing work (the skip-if-gated contract is what makes an unattended run safe — the property band 82 relies on).

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ covers a two-domain batch asserting only ungated topics gain gates and a re-run is a no-op; the progress log records the starting and ending gated/245 count for the domains touched.
